### Model arguments

Model arguments.

::::: {.arg-table role="table"}
:::: {.arg-row .arg-head role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="columnheader"}
Name
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="columnheader"}
Description
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="columnheader"}
Attributes
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--model`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Pretrained model in pkl format. If not provided, the model will be trained on the reference data and --reference should be provided.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`file`

[Example]{.arg-key} `"pretrained_model.pkl"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--n_estimators`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Number of trees in the random forest.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`integer`

[Default]{.arg-key} `100`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--max_depth`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Maximum depth of the trees in the random forest.
If not provided, the nodes are expanded until all leaves only contain a single sample.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`integer`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--criterion`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
The function to measure the quality of a split.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`

[Default]{.arg-key} `"gini"`

[Choices]{.arg-key} `"gini"`, `"entropy"`, `"log_loss"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--class_weight`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Weights associated with classes.
The `balanced` mode uses the values of y to automatically adjust weights inversely proportional to class frequencies in the input data.
The `balanced_subsample` mode is the same as `balanced` except that weights are computed based on the bootstrap sample for every tree grown.
The `uniform` mode gives all classes a weight  of one.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`

[Default]{.arg-key} `"balanced_subsample"`

[Choices]{.arg-key} `"balanced"`, `"balanced_subsample"`, `"uniform"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--max_features`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
The number of features to consider when looking for the best split. The value can either be a positive integer or one of `sqrt`, `log2` or `all`.
If integer: consider max_features features at each split.
If `sqrt`: max_features is the squareroot of all input features.
If `log2`: max_features is the log2 of all input features.
If `all`: max features equals all input features.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`

[Default]{.arg-key} `"200"`
:::
::::
:::::

## Example commands

You can run the pipeline using `nextflow run`.

### View help

You can use `--help` as a parameter to get an overview of the possible parameters.

```bash
nextflow run openpipelines-bio/openpipeline \
  -r v4.2.0 -latest \
  -main-script target/nextflow/annotate/random_forest_annotation/main.nf \
  --help
```

### Run command

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" title="Create a params.yaml"}
The command below reads this component's arguments from a `params.yaml` file. To create one:

- generate it with the form on [Viash Hub](https://www.viash-hub.com/packages/openpipeline/v4.2.0/components/annotate/random_forest_annotation);
- see examples of using params files in the [guides](/guides/index.qmd);
- run several samples in one go with a [`param_list`](/guides/process-many-samples.qmd).
:::

Run locally with:

```bash
nextflow run openpipelines-bio/openpipeline \
  -r v4.2.0 -latest \
  -profile docker \
  -main-script target/nextflow/annotate/random_forest_annotation/main.nf \
  -params-file params.yaml
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" title="Other backends and platforms"}
Replace `-profile docker` with `-profile podman` or `-profile singularity` depending on the desired backend. To run on Seqera Platform or through Viash Hub, see the [guides](/guides/index.qmd).
:::
